analysis: The PR is documentation-only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The supplied units are base_text excerpts (base lines 368-1178) of the modified file. The visible patch excerpt changes the `sandbox` row to say `setup` requires approval from the Darkbloom Sandbox waitlist, adds a `waitlist` anchor reference, and adds head-only ranges (e.g. head 1635-1724) that are not visible in the supplied units. I examined the base context: model switch/drain, logout and token revocation (bearer token to /v1/device/revoke, only HTTP 204 confirms, no redirects, issuer-bound; A-008, T-053), the cluster gpu-limit boundary (TB-014, A-020, T-062: terminal-only, confirmation plus administrator prompt), update/rollback and enroll/unenroll. The unchanged text is consistent with those threat model entries and introduces no contradiction. The sandbox row change is a gating statement, not a security control, in a documented flow. TB-013/T-061 covers the installer download and run as the Mac's owner, and a waitlist approval does not replace the installer integrity concerns recorded there. The patch excerpt is truncated and the head-side additions (waitlist section, head 1360-1385, 1635-1724) are not in the supplied units, so I cannot verify whether the new `darkbloom waitlist` documentation describes new credential, token or network handling (a new CLI-to-service trust boundary, possibly TB-013-adjacent). The next pass should review that head text if it is supplied, for what the waitlist command sends, how it is authenticated, and whether approval is enforced server-side or only client-side. No concrete regression is identifiable from the supplied evidence.
